# Preconditions and test data from framework recipes

<!-- Generated by `bun run qa:arrange --catalog` from framework/setup/recipes.ts. Change the recipe, not this file. -->

**Arrange with the framework, act by hand.** Every start state a manual run, bug repro, exploration or spec needs (a
signed-in customer, a cart, a coupon, an order, a locked account) comes from a recipe below, and every value typed into
the app (cards, addresses, registrations) from the framework. Only the steps under test are performed in the browser
or over the API by hand. Do not click through registration, cart or checkout to reach a start state, and do not make up data.

## How to arrange a precondition

| From | How |
| --- | --- |
| a manual test case | `bun run qa:arrange --case TC-… --name <session>`, which runs the case's `setup` |
| a recipe | `bun run qa:arrange <recipe> --name <session> [param=value …]` |
| a script (bug repro, probe) | `await arrange(request, '<recipe>', { … })` from `@setup/recipes` |
| a spec | the `arrange` fixture: `await arrange('<recipe>', { … })` acts as the test's signed-in customer |
| the list | `bun run qa:arrange --list` |

The CLI starts ShopLite as `TEST_ENV` when it is not running and prints JSON: `user` (email, password), `data` (what it
created, with ids), `testData` (cards, an address, a fresh registration) and `next`: the playwright-cli commands that
open the state (`open`, `state-load out/sessions/<session>.json` when signed in, `goto <route>`). It also saves
`out/sessions/<session>.arranged.json`. `--defects <ids|all|none>` switches the seeded defects (app/defects.ts).
Each session gets its own recipe run: data is never shared between sessions or tests.

## Recipe: guest

Signed out; creates nothing. Registration, sign-in and public pages from scratch.

- Creates data: no (runs on live too)
- Steps start on: `#/`
- Typical for: FEAT-AUTH, FEAT-CATALOG, BR-AUTH-01
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange guest --name <session>`

No parameters.

## Recipe: returning-customer

Signed in as the saved returning customer (order history); creates nothing. This is the only signed-in state on live. Read-only use.

- Creates data: no (runs on live too)
- Steps start on: `#/orders`
- Typical for: FEAT-ORDERS
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange returning-customer --name <session>`

No parameters.

## Recipe: customer

A freshly registered customer with an empty cart; signed in, or signed out with its credentials to type.

- Creates data: yes (not allowed on a read-only environment)
- Steps start on: `#/ (signed in) · #/login (signed out)`
- Typical for: FEAT-AUTH, BR-AUTH-02
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange customer --name <session> signedIn=false`

| Param | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `signedIn` | boolean | `true` | false: the browser starts signed out; sign in with user.email / user.password |

## Recipe: locked-out

A customer locked by 5 failed sign-ins (verified: the right password is refused); signed out.

- Creates data: yes (not allowed on a read-only environment)
- Steps start on: `#/login`
- Typical for: BR-AUTH-02
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange locked-out --name <session>`

No parameters.

## Recipe: product

A signed-in customer and a fresh product of their own (price, stock), not yet in the cart.

- Creates data: yes (not allowed on a read-only environment)
- Steps start on: `#/product/<product.id>`
- Typical for: FEAT-CATALOG, FEAT-CART, BR-CART-01, BR-CART-02
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange product --name <session> priceCents=1500 stock=0`

| Param | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `priceCents` | number | `1000` | unit price of a fresh product, in cents |
| `stock` | number | `50` | its stock (0 = out of stock) |

## Recipe: cart

A signed-in customer with a fresh product in the cart, optionally with an existing coupon code applied.

- Creates data: yes (not allowed on a read-only environment)
- Steps start on: `#/cart`
- Typical for: FEAT-CART, FEAT-CHECKOUT, BR-CART-01, BR-SHIP-01, BR-PAY-01, BR-COUP-02
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange cart --name <session> priceCents=5000 stock=10 quantity=1`

| Param | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `priceCents` | number | `1000` | unit price of a fresh product, in cents |
| `stock` | number | `50` | its stock (0 = out of stock) |
| `quantity` | number | `1` | units of it in the cart |
| `coupon` | string | none | a code to apply, e.g. WELCOME10 (seeded). For a custom coupon use the `coupon` recipe |

## Recipe: coupon

A coupon of its own shape (kind, value, minimum, cap, expired) and a cart to try it on; applied or not.

- Creates data: yes (not allowed on a read-only environment)
- Steps start on: `#/cart`
- Typical for: FEAT-COUPON, BR-COUP-01, BR-COUP-02, BR-COUP-03, BR-COUP-04
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange coupon --name <session> kind=fixed value=500 minSubtotalCents=3000 priceCents=2000 quantity=2 applied=true`

| Param | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `priceCents` | number | `1000` | unit price of a fresh product, in cents |
| `stock` | number | `50` | its stock (0 = out of stock) |
| `quantity` | number | `1` | units of it in the cart |
| `kind` | percent \| fixed | `percent` | percent off, or a fixed amount in cents |
| `value` | number | `10` | percent, or cents for `fixed` |
| `minSubtotalCents` | number | `0` | the minimum subtotal it needs |
| `maxDiscountCents` | number | none | the discount cap |
| `expired` | boolean | `false` | expired yesterday |
| `applied` | boolean | `false` | apply it to the cart (an expired one cannot be) |

## Recipe: order

A signed-in customer with an order of a fresh product: placed, shipped (by the admin) or cancelled.

- Creates data: yes (not allowed on a read-only environment)
- Steps start on: `#/orders/<order.id>`
- Typical for: FEAT-ORDERS, BR-ORD-01, BR-ORD-02, BR-ORD-03
- Example: `bun run qa:arrange order --name <session> stock=5 status=shipped`

| Param | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `priceCents` | number | `1000` | unit price of a fresh product, in cents |
| `stock` | number | `50` | its stock (0 = out of stock) |
| `quantity` | number | `1` | units of it in the cart |
| `status` | placed \| shipped \| cancelled | `placed` | the order status to leave it in |

## Test data

Cards (mock gateway, BR-PAY-01) are `testData.cards` in the CLI output and `Cards` from `@data/cards` in code. Expiry dates
move with the calendar, so take them from the output, never from a document:

| Card | Number | CVC | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `VALID` | `4242424242424242` | `123` | approved (BR-PAY-01) |
| `DECLINED` | `4000000000000002` | `123` | declined by the gateway: "The card was declined" |
| `INVALID_NUMBER` | `4242424242424241` | `123` | fails the Luhn check |
| `EXPIRED` | `4242424242424242` | `123` | expired at the end of last month |

- **Addresses:** `testData.address` (`newAddress()` from `@data/people`) is a valid US address.
- **Registrations:** `testData.registration` (`newRegistration()`) gives a unique `qa.…@example.test` email and a password
  valid under BR-AUTH-01.
- **Codes:** `uniqueSku()`, `uniqueCouponCode()` for anything a script creates itself.
- **Saved accounts:** `returning-customer` (read-only, all environments), `admin` (used by the seed only). Credentials
  are encrypted in `env/`; recipes sign in for you.
- **Seeded catalog data** (products, `WELCOME10`, `SUMMER20`, `BIGSPENDER`) is shared and read-only. A run that
  changes stock or applies its own kind of coupon uses a recipe instead.

## When no recipe fits

1. Compose the state in a script from `arrange()`, `Seed` (`@setup/seed`) and the `@api` helpers, for example in
   `out/bugs/<DEF-id>/repro.ts`. Never go through the UI.
2. Report `RECIPE_MISSING: <the state>`. `test-author` then adds a recipe to `framework/setup/recipes.ts` (reviewed like
   any framework code) and `bun run qa:arrange --catalog` regenerates this document.
3. A state the API cannot reach (time passing, a third-party outage) is a testability gap. Report it, do not click
   around it.
